record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For an unforced one-dimensional fourth-order degenerate lubrication equation for a thin film or Hele-Shaw neck, with film height h and mobility depending on a power of h, can one prove finite-time singularity formation without imposing special forcing boundary conditions?

evidence.quote: a proof of singularity formation for an unforced system

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation
   h_t + (h^n h_{xxx})_x = 0,   x ∈ I, t > 0,
modeling, in the lubrication approximation, the evolution of the height h(x,t) ≥ 0 of a thin viscous film or of the neck thickness in a Hele-Shaw cell driven by surface tension, where n > 0 is a fixed mobility exponent. Consider the "unforced" setting: either the equation is posed on the real line (or on a periodic interval) with smooth, nonnegative, compactly supported (or periodic) initial data h(·,0) = h_0, or on a bounded interval I with homogeneous (non-driving) boundary conditions that do not inject mass, momentum, or pressure (so, in particular, no prescribed positive pressure jump or fixed positive boundary heights driving a pinch-off).

Prove (or disprove) that for some range of mobility exponents n > 0 and for some class of smooth nonnegative initial data h_0, there exist solutions h(x,t) of the above equation that develop a finite-time singularity, in the sense that
   inf_{x} h(x,t) → 0   as t ↑ T*   for some finite T* < ∞,
without imposing any forcing through the boundary conditions or external terms.
artifact.category_tag: Thin-film lubrication equations and singularity formation
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous finite-time singularity (pinch-off) proofs for the 1D fourth-order lubrication / Hele-Shaw neck equation have so far required driving boundary conditions: Constantin–Elgindi–Nguyen–Vicol (Comm. Math. Phys. 2018) prove pinch-off in finite or infinite time for the Hele-Shaw neck equation under boundary conditions h(±1,t)=1 and h_{xx}(±1,t)=P>2, which is a forced setting. For long-wave unstable variants (with a destabilizing lower-order term) finite-time blow-up of weak solutions is known. For the genuinely unforced surface-tension-driven thin-film/Hele-Shaw equation with mobility h^n, a proof of finite-time singularity formation without special forcing boundary conditions does not appear in the literature and remains an open problem actively discussed in recent work on touchdown singularities.

status_evidence.title: On Singularity Formation in a Hele-Shaw Model
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary conditions h(±1,t)=1 and ∂_x^2 h(±1,t)=P>0; for P>2 the solution pinches off in finite or infinite time.
status_evidence.claim: Existing pinch-off proof requires forcing boundary conditions (prescribed positive pressure jump P>2).

status_evidence.title: Touchdown-singularity formation and criticality in the thin-film equation
status_evidence.snippet: Touchdown scenarios are available up to certain mobility exponents; characterization of finite-time singularity formation in the unforced thin-film equation remains an active research area.
status_evidence.claim: The question of unforced finite-time singularity formation in thin-film/lubrication equations remains open in general.
